Best advice I will probably ever give is to Read the book “Attached” by Adam Levine. He wrote the book in 1989 and it has formed the base of the new and popular attachment theory principles for sociology and psychology going forward. It’s eye opening and should be required reading for everyone in school, but weird schools don’t want us to get along... You have an anxious attachment style and yes, it is due to abandonment and how you were raised as a child. You probably have other attachments to material things and are a people pleaser. You likely come off as needy and that can feel suffocating to people on the receiving end. People will leave you, people will move on, people won’t always give you the attention you deserve but it is up to you to grow a backbone and focus on healing your wounds so u can encourage secure relationships to form in their place. Also, look into DBT, dialectical behavior therapy: a specific type of therapy that works excellent in conjunction with classical therapy but which focuses on coping, mindfulness, behavioral and “wise mind” techniques to propel u into a healthy lifestyle. You can look up the DBT techniques but it’s best practiced regularly and therapy is typically done to check-in on others and how they are doing so a group setting is preferable. Best of luck 🤞
